added_lines: a note from fr. over the past twenty years, ireland has undergone an extraordinary transformation. we have moved from a society deeply rooted in christianity to one increasingly shaped by secular values. as one english commentator recently remarked, ireland has gone from organising itself around the catholic religion to organising itself around the “woke religion." we see this in changing attitudes towards the sacredness of human life, marriage, family and the place of christianity in public life. there was a time when people looked to the gospel, the 10 commandments and the teachings of the church as their moral compass. today, many look instead to politicians, legislators and the laws of the land. the assumption seems to be that if something is legal, it must be morally right. but since when did a majority vote determine what is good or evil? let us not forget nazi germany, where appalling injustices were given the force of law and accepted or tolerated by so many. history reminds us that something can be perfectly legal and yet profoundly immoral. the law of the land is not necessarily the law of god. in this sunday's gospel, jesus tells us: “give back to caesar what belongs to caesar and to god what belongs to god." jesus asks for a coin: “whose image is this?" “caesar's,” they reply. but there is a deeper question. if the coin bears caesar's image, whose image do you and i bear? genesis gives us the answer: we are created in the image and likeness of god. jesus is not telling us to disregard civil authority. we have a christian responsibility to be good citizens, pay our taxes, respect just laws and contribute to the common good. but caesar is not god. governments have legitimate authority, but that authority has limits. when the laws of the state conflict with god's law, our first allegiance must always be to god. as st peter reminds us,“we must obey god rather than men." the coin belongs to caesar because it bears his image. but we belong to god because we bear his image. god doesn't simply want an hour on sunday or a few prayers. he wants our hearts, our minds and our whole lives. perhaps that is the real challenge of today's gospel: who ultimately governs my life? caesar, with his changing laws and values, or god, whose truth never changes? so who do i belong to caesar? (our government) or do i belong to god? give caesar what is rightly his, but never give caesar what belongs to god.
